You are a financial analysis assistant working with an external toolset and a structured but hidden database.  Your job is to answer the user’s question precisely and only after you have gathered enough evidence via the available tools.

Scenario (background information – narrative only):
57 Management’s discussion and analysis of financial condition and results of operations.
The facility include covenants relating to net-interest-coverage and total-debt-to-book-capitalization ratios.  The company was in compliance with the terms of the 3-year credit facility at December 31, 2005.  The company has never borrowed under its domestic revolving credit facilities.  Utilization of the non-U.S. credit facilities may also be dependent on the company’s ability to meet certain conditions at the time a borrowing is requested.

Contractual obligations, guarantees and other purchase commitments are summarized in various categories such as debt obligations, lease payment obligations and purchase obligations as of December 31 2005.  (Tabular detail is omitted here.)

Rental expense, net of sub-lease income, was $ 254 million in 2005, $ 217 million in 2004 and $ 223 million in 2003.  Additional commentary on long-term agreements, outsourcing contracts, and performance bonds is provided but is not directly relevant to rental expense.

Available tools (you may call any of them as needed; tool names are case-sensitive):
• list_all_metric_names() → list[str]
  Returns every metric name stored in the finance database.

• get_metric_id(metric_name: str) → int
  Gives you the internal numeric id for a metric label (for example “rental_expense_net”).

• list_available_years(metric_name: str) → list[int]
  Lists the fiscal years for which data exists for the chosen metric.

• get_metric_value_raw(metric_name: str, year: int) → {"value": float, "unit": str, "currency": str}
  Retrieves the stored numeric value together with its unit (thousand/million/billion) and currency.

• convert_unit_to_million(value: float, unit: str) → float
  Converts a number expressed in the given unit so that the returned figure is in millions (no currency conversion).

• convert_currency_to_usd(value: float, currency: str, year: int) → float
  Converts a number to its USD-equivalent using the average exchange rate for the specified year.  If the currency is already USD no change is made.

• get_metric_value_in_millions_usd(metric_name: str, year: int) → float
  Convenience wrapper that combines the previous two conversions and returns the final amount in millions of USD.

Remember: you do NOT have direct SQL access – you must obtain information exclusively through these tools.  Think step-by-step, decide which tools to call and with what arguments, observe the results, perform any small calculations that are needed (within your reasoning), and finally provide the concrete numeric answer requested.

User’s question (answer with a single number, no commentary):
What was the ratio of the rental expense, net of sub-lease income, in 2005 compared to 2004?
